about.title: About the Atlas
about.description: Atlas of Today’s World is an independent encyclopedia of the present, built around an interactive 3D globe.
about.intro: Atlas of Today’s World is an independent encyclopedia of the present. Instead of an A–Z list, it starts from a satellite globe: you spin it, click a country, and the Atlas opens that country’s profile together with the portrait of the world region it belongs to. News opens inside the same map, so the geographic context never disappears.
about.dataText: Country borders and names come from Natural Earth. The data layers are imported in bulk from Our World in Data and refreshed with a single command, so a yearly update takes minutes rather than manual editing:
about.editorialText: Region portraits, country profiles and news are written by the Atlas team in the Atlas’s own editorial system, where every change goes through review before it is published.
about.missionText: Atlas of Today’s World helps anyone understand today’s world in its geographic context — free to read, without advertising and without an account. We are a non-profit, non-governmental organization registered in the Czech Republic since 2016, supported by our readers through Atlas Patrons.
about.whoText: {legalName}, a registered association (spolek) under Czech law, company ID (IČO) {companyId}, {address}. Contact: {email}.
about.standardsText: Every article names its author and shows when it was published and last updated. Facts link to their sources, and every number comes with the year and the institution that measured it. Each change is reviewed by an editor before it is published. If you find a mistake, write to {email}: we correct errors openly and update the article’s date.
about.citeText: Atlas of Today’s World, “page title”, page URL (date of access). Data layers can also be cited with their original source, which every page names.
about.machineTitle: For researchers, search engines and AI tools
about.machineText: The Atlas is open to search engines and AI assistants. A Markdown overview for language models is at /llms.txt (full text at /llms-full.txt), every article has a Markdown version (add .md to its address), and new articles appear in our RSS and Atom feeds.

faq.question: Will the content be free for everyone?
faq.answer: Our primary mission is to give everyone a chance to reflect on the situation in our world. Therefore, our encyclopedia will be fully open-access to any reader all over the world. The role of the membership community is to support this mission.

faq.question: Are you a registered nonprofit organisation?
faq.answer: Our project grew out of the Online Encyclopedia of Migration, a non-profit, non-governmental organisation that has been registered in the Czech Republic since 2016 (we are officially called Online Encyklopedie Migrace, z.s.). Within Czech legislation, we are not permitted to make any profit.

faq.question: How can I cancel or change my monthly donation?
faq.answer: You can cancel your monthly donation anytime via Stripe. The link is available below the Donate & Join button, in your initial registration email, and at the bottom of each members-only newsletter. Alternatively, you can email us at {email}, and we will help you. Similarly, you can change your initial one-time donation to a monthly donation by following the same steps.
